Algebra I · Lesson 2.6

Expressions with Many Variables

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Everything from 2.5 still works when more than one letter is in view. Take 8ab+9ab8ab+9ab. The coefficients add the 2.4 way, 8+9=178+9=17, so 8ab+9ab=17ab8ab+9ab=17ab, and the abab stays as it is. The one new question is what counts as the same kind of term, now that a single term can carry several letters.

Problem
Combine 7st+6st7st+6st into one term. Type its coefficient.
Show a hint
  • stst is one variable part, so this is a single family.
  • Add the coefficients, the 2.4 way.
Show the full solution
stst is one variable part, so the coefficients add, 7+6=137+6=13​. Two letters in a term does not make it two families. The whole variable part is what has to match.
Key idea
A single term can contain several letters. Terms like abab, 2mn2mn, and 5rst5rst are one term each, a coefficient times a product of letters. Multiplication can be done in any order, the 1.3 move, so the order of letters inside a term does not matter. That makes abab and baba the same term, and mnmn and nmnm the same term.
Key idea
Like terms match the whole variable part. Two terms are like only when their entire variable part is identical, every letter and its power. So 4jk4jk and 9jk9jk are like and combine to 13jk13jk. But 4jk4jk and 4j4j are unlike, and so are 4jk4jk and 4j2k4j2k, since j2j2 means j⋅jj⋅j, the 1.5 reading. Writing 6ab+4a=10ab6ab+4a=10ab would require the two sides to agree at every input, the 1.4 test, and they do not. The figure shows this as tile shapes.
Problem
A classmate rewrote 5cd+5c5cd+5c as 10cd10cd, adding the coefficients as if the terms matched. Evaluate the original 5cd+5c5cd+5c at c=2, d=4c=2, d=4. Type the value.
Show a hint
  • Are 5cd5cd and 5c5c really like terms? Compare their variable parts.
  • Put c=2, d=4c=2, d=4 into the original 5cd+5c5cd+5c, one letter at a time.
Show the full solution
Substitute into the original. 5cd=5⋅2⋅4=405cd=5⋅2⋅4=40 and 5c=5⋅2=105c=5⋅2=10, so the value is 40+10=5040+10=50​. The classmate's 10cd10cd gives 8080 at the same input, and one input with two different outputs proves 5cd5cd and 5c5c are unlike.
Key idea
Combine one family at a time. To simplify, sweep the expression once for each distinct variable part, add the coefficients in that family, and keep the variable part unchanged. This is the 2.4 count with more letters in view. A minus sign belongs to the term right after it, so −3wv−3wv contributes −3−3 to the vwvw family once you use wv=vwwv=vw from 1.3.
Problem
Simplify 11mn+9m−5nm11mn+9m−5nm by combining like terms. Type the coefficient of the mnmn term.
Show a hint
  • nmnm is the same variable part as mnmn, so the order does not matter.
  • The minus travels with its term into the mnmn family; the 9m9m is a different family.
Show the full solution
Read nmnm as mnmn, so 11mn−5mn=6mn11mn−5mn=6mn, and the 9m9m is a separate family. The coefficient is 66​. Order inside a term is free, so a backward-written term still joins its family, and its minus sign comes with it.
Key idea
A distributed factor multiplies every term. When a factor with a letter in it multiplies a sum, it multiplies each term inside, the 2.1 move. So 2h(3k+4m)=6hk+8hm2h(3k+4m)=6hk+8hm, with the hh in both products. If the letter were left off one term, the two expressions would disagree on a test input.
Problem
Distribute 8r(2s+t)8r(2s+t). Type the coefficient of the rsrs term.
Show a hint
  • The 8r8r multiplies every term inside the parentheses.
  • You only need the term that has rr and ss.
Show the full solution
8r⋅2s=16rs8r⋅2s=16rs and 8r⋅t=8rt8r⋅t=8rt, so the rsrs coefficient is 1616​. The 8r8r multiplies both terms inside, not just the first.
Problem
Simplify 2(4uv+5v)+7uv2(4uv+5v)+7uv by distributing then combining like terms. Type the coefficient of the uvuv term.
Show a hint
  • Distribute the 22 across both terms inside first.
  • Only the uvuv terms combine; the plain vv term is a different family.
Show the full solution
Distribute first, 2(4uv+5v)=8uv+10v2(4uv+5v)=8uv+10v. Only the uvuv terms combine, 8uv+7uv=15uv8uv+7uv=15uv, so the coefficient is 1515​. The 10v10v has a different variable part, so it never joins the uvuv count.
Key idea
Factor out everything shared. The greatest common factor is the number GCD times each letter that appears in every term. That is the full scan from 2.3. Pull it to the front, and each leftover keeps its sign. For 6mn+9mp6mn+9mp the number GCD is 33 and only mm is in both terms, so 6mn+9mp=3m(2n+3p)6mn+9mp=3m(2n+3p). The nn and pp are not shared, so they stay inside.
Problem
Find the greatest common factor of the terms in 8pqr+12pqs8pqr+12pqs, typed like 2xy2xy, the number first and the letters in alphabetical order.
Show a hint
  • Take the GCD of 88 and 1212 first.
  • Which letters appear in BOTH terms? Only those come out front.
Show the full solution
The GCD of 88 and 1212 is 44, and pp and qq are the letters sitting in both terms, so the GCF is 4pq4pq​. The rr and ss each appear in only one term, so neither can come out front.
Key idea
Substitute one letter at a time. To evaluate a multi-variable expression, replace each letter with its given value, then do the arithmetic exactly as in 1.6. A term like 4mn4mn needs both values, 4⋅m⋅n4⋅m⋅n, so dropping either letter is the common mistake.
Problem
Evaluate 4gh−2g+h4gh−2g+h at g=5, h=2g=5, h=2. Type the value.
Show a hint
  • 4gh4gh needs both letters, so 4⋅g⋅h4⋅g⋅h.
  • Handle the −2g−2g and +h+h after the 4gh4gh term.
Show the full solution
4⋅5⋅2=404⋅5⋅2=40, then −2⋅5=−10−2⋅5=−10 and +2+2, so 40−10+2=3240−10+2=32​. A term like 4gh4gh needs both values, and reading it as 4g4g drops the hh.
Problem
Simplify 2d(4e+f)+9de2d(4e+f)+9de by distributing and combining, then evaluate the result at d=2, e=1, f=5d=2, e=1, f=5. Type the value.
Show a hint
  • Distribute 2d2d first, keeping the dd on both new terms.
  • Combine the dede terms, then substitute d=2, e=1, f=5d=2, e=1, f=5.
Show the full solution
Distribute, 2d(4e+f)=8de+2df2d(4e+f)=8de+2df, then combine, 8de+9de=17de8de+9de=17de. Now substitute, 17⋅2⋅1=3417⋅2⋅1=34 and 2⋅2⋅5=202⋅2⋅5=20, so 34+20=5434+20=54​. The dd has to stay on both new terms, and dede and dfdf are different families, so they never merge.
Fun fact
Two terms are like only when their whole variable part matches, every letter and its power. A shared coefficient or a single shared letter is not enough, which is why 4ab4ab and 4a4a never combine.

That caps Chapter 2. Distribute, combine, factor, and evaluate are the whole toolkit, and none of them changed when several letters came into view. Only the like-term rule widened, since the variable part now has to match in full. Chapter 3 turns to exponents, the shorthand for a letter multiplied by itself over and over, along with the rules that come with them.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Combine 5jk+9jk5jk+9jk. Type the coefficient.
Show the solution
jkjk is one variable part, so the coefficients add, 5+9=145+9=14​.
Practice
Combine 7gh+8hg7gh+8hg. Type the coefficient.
Show the solution
hghg and ghgh are the same variable part, so both terms sit in one family and 7+8=157+8=15​. Flipping the letters inside a term does not make a new family.
Practice
After combining like terms in 5mp+2m+4mp5mp+2m+4mp, how many terms remain?
Show the solution
The mpmp family gives 5+4=9mp5+4=9mp, and 2m2m stands on its own, so 22​ terms remain. The 2m2m has a different variable part, so it never joins the mpmp count.
Practice
Are 6ab6ab and 6a6a like terms? Type yes or no.
Show the solution
The variable parts are abab and aa, and those differ, so nono​. A shared coefficient and one shared letter are not enough, since the whole variable part has to match.
Practice
Evaluate 4pq+3p4pq+3p at p=2, q=5p=2, q=5. Type the value.
Show the solution
4⋅2⋅5=404⋅2⋅5=40 and 3⋅2=63⋅2=6, so 40+6=4640+6=46​. The 4pq4pq term needs both values, and reading it as 4p4p drops the qq.
Practice
Evaluate 2mn+4m−n2mn+4m−n at m=3, n=1m=3, n=1. Type the value.
Show the solution
2⋅3⋅1=62⋅3⋅1=6, 4⋅3=124⋅3=12, and the last term is −1−1, so 6+12−1=176+12−1=17​. The 2mn2mn term needs both values, not just the mm.
Practice
Distribute 2a(4b+3c)2a(4b+3c). Type the coefficient of the abab term.
Show the solution
2a⋅4b=8ab2a⋅4b=8ab, so the abab coefficient is 88​. The 2a2a multiplies both terms inside, not just the first.
Practice
Distribute 5m(2n+4p)5m(2n+4p). Type the coefficient of the mpmp term.
Show the solution
The mpmp term comes from 5m⋅4p=20mp5m⋅4p=20mp, so the coefficient is 2020​. The other product, 5m⋅2n=10mn5m⋅2n=10mn, is a different family.
Practice
Simplify 3r(s+2)+4rs3r(s+2)+4rs. Type the coefficient of the rsrs term.
Show the solution
Distribute, 3r(s+2)=3rs+6r3r(s+2)=3rs+6r. Only the rsrs terms combine, 3rs+4rs=7rs3rs+4rs=7rs, so the coefficient is 77​. The 6r6r has no ss, so it stays out of the rsrs count.
Practice
Factor 8ab+12ac8ab+12ac fully. Type the greatest common factor pulled out front, written like 5x5x (number first, letters alphabetical).
Show the solution
The GCD of 88 and 1212 is 44, and aa is the only letter in both terms, so the GCF is 4a4a​. The bb and cc each appear once, so neither comes out front.
Practice
Factor 6cdh+15cdk6cdh+15cdk fully. Type the greatest common factor, written like 2xy2xy (number first, letters alphabetical).
Show the solution
The GCD of 66 and 1515 is 33, and both cc and dd sit in every term, so the GCF is 3cd3cd​. The hh and kk each appear in only one term, so they stay inside.
Practice
Evaluate 5st−2s+t5st−2s+t at s=2, t=3s=2, t=3. Type the value.
Show the solution
5⋅2⋅3=305⋅2⋅3=30, −2⋅2=−4−2⋅2=−4, and +3+3, so 30−4+3=2930−4+3=29​. The 5st5st term needs both values, and reading it as 5s5s drops the tt.
